task.description:
SECURITY-REVIEWER passed Step 2c (see step-02c-security-reviewer.json's result block and the full findings in handoffs/WF02-REQ197-20260830/security-review-req197-findings.md). Scope test was independently re-run: only lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex is touched in production code, no route/migration/secret. All applicable invariants (INV-8 only; INV-1..7 not-applicable) passed. Your scope is idiomatic OTP usage, decision-record/design-doc consistency, and scope creep -- read the real diff and the approved design (lib/letflow/design/req197-expr-arithmetic-and-errors.md) in full before verdict.

THREE ITEMS CARRIED FORWARD FROM SECURITY-REVIEWER, EACH NEEDING YOUR EXPLICIT DECISION OR AWARENESS (do not let any of these get silently accepted or silently expanded without a stated decision):

(a) OQ-1 DEFERRAL -- NEEDS YOUR EXPLICIT SIGN-OFF. ELIXIR-DEV implemented the design's own stated safe fallback: a single unsigned `:infinity` marker for float division by a zero divisor (any dividend, including 0.0/0.0), rather than the full signed-infinity/NaN 3-way split design section 4.3/4.6 reasons about. SECURITY-REVIEWER's independent analysis (expr.ex:1088, 1109-1120) found this is not merely an incompleteness: `apply_float_arith(:div, _l, r) when r == 0.0` collapses every float division by zero to the same unsigned :infinity regardless of dividend sign, and apply_ordering/3 treats :infinity as the greatest possible value in every comparison. Concretely: a gateway condition of the form `amount / 0.0 > threshold` evaluates true for BOTH a large positive amount AND a large-magnitude NEGATIVE amount, where a correctly-signed implementation would put the negative case at -infinity (false for any finite positive threshold) -- a real, demonstrable gateway-branch-decision divergence for a plausible tenant input, not a hypothetical corner case. SECURITY-REVIEWER found this does NOT cross any INV-1..INV-8 boundary (a tenant's own process definition producing a wrong-but-internally-consistent decision on that tenant's own data; no cross-tenant leakage, no crash, no secret/SQL/auth issue) -- so it is not a SECURITY-REVIEWER BLOCKER, but it IS a substantive correctness question for gateway behavior that you must explicitly decide: accept the unsigned-:infinity-only fallback as REQ-197's final implemented shape (with the sign-flip behavior above understood and accepted), or send this back requesting the fuller signed/NaN split with new AC-level test coverage (none exists today for this case).

(b) OQ-4 -- AWARENESS ONLY, NOT BLOCKING. Negative-operand integer division/modulo (e.g. -7/2, -7 % 2) uses Elixir's native `div/2`/`rem/2` semantics directly (truncate-toward-zero) with no new type/AST surface -- the design's own reasoned choice, not independently verified against R-Co's real evaluator.zig, and no acceptance criterion exercises a negative-operand case. No action requested beyond your awareness.

(c) DESIGN-PREFERENCE DEVIATION (your own idiom/code-quality scope, not SECURITY-REVIEWER's) -- `parse_strict/1` was given its OWN position-tracking tokenizer/parser pair (`tokenize_positioned/1`, `do_tokenize_positioned/4`, `parse_or_p/2`..`parse_primary_p/2`), structurally mirroring the existing `tokenize/1`+`parse_or/1`..`parse_primary/1` pair one-for-one, rather than threading position bookkeeping through the single existing implementation as design doc section 6.2 states as its stated preference ('share one underlying tokenizer and one underlying grammar implementation'). ELIXIR-DEV's stated rationale (expr.ex:401-418): avoid touching the existing tokenizer's delicate escape-handling code (two prior bug-fix histories, ISS-0086/ISS-0087) and guarantee `parse/1`'s outer shape stays byte-for-byte safe. SECURITY-REVIEWER confirmed `parse_strict/1` is not on `evaluate_condition/2`'s call graph today (inert new surface). Please review this duplication for idiom/maintainability acceptability -- accept it as a reasonable lower-risk tradeoff, or request the shared-implementation approach the design doc actually specified.
acceptance_criteria: Confirm Letflow.Engine.Expr's new code (arith_op(), {:arith, ...}/{:neg, ...} AST nodes, parse_additive/parse_multiplicative/parse_unary, parse_strict/1 and its tokenizer/parser pair) follows this codebase's existing conventions -- compare typespec style, error-tuple shape, moduledoc format against the rest of expr.ex.

Confirm no scope creep: only lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex, test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs, test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs, and the design doc are touched -- transition.ex and every other caller of Expr are untouched (confirmed already by SECURITY-REVIEWER's `git diff --stat`, but re-verify).
Decide OQ-1 (item (a) above) explicitly: accept the unsigned-:infinity fallback as final, or send back for the fuller signed/NaN split with new test coverage.
Review item (c)'s parse_strict/1 tokenizer-duplication design-preference deviation and state a verdict: acceptable tradeoff, or request the shared-implementation approach.
Note OQ-4 (item (b)) awareness in your result -- no action required beyond acknowledging it.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.summary:
REVIEWER gate on REQ-197 -- FAIL, 1 BLOCKER (OQ-1 sign-off decided as REQUEST, not ACCEPT). Read lib/letflow/design/req197-expr-arithmetic-and-errors.md in full, handoffs/WF02-REQ197-20260830/security-review-req197-findings.md in full, and lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex in full (not from either report's description of it) before deciding.

SCOPE/IDIOM CHECKS -- all PASS. Confirmed `git diff main...HEAD --stat` scope is unchanged from SECURITY-REVIEWER's own re-verification (only lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex touched in production code). New code's typespec style (@spec on every def/defp, @typedoc on every new @type), error-tuple shape ({:error, {:eval_error, reason}} / {:error, {:parse_error, reason}}, reusing the existing :type_mismatch/:null_in_arithmetic family), and moduledoc format all match the rest of the module and REQ-050's established precedent -- no new convention invented. eval({:arith,...}) and eval({:neg,...}) are added as new clauses parallel in shape to the existing eval({:cmp,...}) clauses, exactly per design §4.1 -- idiomatic, not a bolted-on special case. No supervision-tree concern: expr.ex is a pure, stateless module with no process, no gen_statem/GenServer involved, so the OTP-idiom/supervision-integrity questions in this role's charter (INV-relevant to gen_statem/InstanceSupervisor) are not applicable to this diff at all -- confirmed no new process, no spawn, nothing collapsing per-instance isolation.

NIL-HANDLING RE-VERIFICATION (independent of SECURITY-REVIEWER's trace) -- CONFIRMED, no bypass. Read expr.ex:1005-1030 (the ordering-comparison eval clause) and expr.ex:1146-1155 (evaluate_condition/2's `with {:ok, expr_source} <- ..., {:ok, ast} <- ..., {:ok, true} <- eval(ast, variables) do true else _ -> false end`) directly myself. The new `lv == nil or rv == nil -> {:ok, nil}` branch (checked first, expr.ex:1016-1017) produces a value that fails the literal `{:ok, true}` match in the `with`, falling to `else _ -> false` -- exactly the same external outcome the pre-change `{:error, {:eval_error, {:type_mismatch, ...}}}` path produced (also caught by `else _ -> false`). Also confirmed via transition.ex:660-676 that the sole caller (`evaluate_conditioned_edges/3`) only ever branches on the returned boolean. No route by which nil-propagation flips a gateway edge to taken. SECURITY-REVIEWER's conclusion independently reproduced, not just trusted.

OQ-1 DECISION -- REQUEST the fuller signed-infinity/NaN 3-way split, do NOT accept the unsigned-only fallback as final. Read apply_float_arith/3 (expr.ex:1083-1093) and apply_ordering/3 (expr.ex:1107-1120) directly and confirmed SECURITY-REVIEWER's trace is exactly accurate: `apply_float_arith(:div, _l, r) when r == 0.0, do: {:ok, :infinity}` collapses every float division by a zero divisor to one unsigned marker regardless of dividend sign, and `apply_ordering/3`'s `l == :infinity or r == :infinity` branch (expr.ex:1109-1115) then treats that marker as the greatest possible value unconditionally -- so `amount / 0.0 > threshold` is `true` for both a large positive `amount` and a large-magnitude NEGATIVE `amount`, where IEEE-correct signed semantics would place the negative case at -infinity (false for any finite positive threshold). This is a real, demonstrable gateway-branch-decision divergence for a plausible tenant input (a negative-amount edge case dividing by a zero-valued divisor), not a hypothetical corner case -- reproduced the trace myself rather than taking SECURITY-REVIEWER's word for it.

Investigated whether native Elixir/Erlang float division already produces signed infinity (the premise floated as a way to remove the R-Co-verification blocker entirely) -- no Elixir/Erlang toolchain is reachable on this host (`elixir`/`erl` both absent, consistent with this project's documented sandbox limits), so this could not be empirically re-run. Reasoning from established, well-documented BEAM semantics instead (the design doc's own §4.3 already states this correctly, and it is not in dispute): the BEAM's native float arithmetic operators (`/`, and float overflow generally) raise `ArithmeticError` (`badarith`) rather than ever constructing an IEEE-754 infinity or NaN float term -- Erlang/BEAM floats are deliberately restricted to finite values by the VM, unlike C/Python/Zig's native IEEE-754-conformant runtimes. So there is no native `1.0/0.0`-shaped shortcut that already does the right (signed) thing; the hand-rolled sentinel-construction approach the design already chose is necessary, not optional, and this part of OQ-1's premise does not change the decision.

What DOES change the decision: the reason OQ-1 was deferred -- that R-Co's real src/expr/evaluator.zig is unreachable from this sandbox and the signed/NaN behaviour is therefore "unverified" -- does not actually apply to the SIGN determination itself. IEEE 754 division-by-zero sign/NaN rules (sign(dividend)/0.0 -> +-infinity matching the dividend's sign; 0.0/0.0 -> NaN) are a fixed mathematical standard, not an R-Co-specific implementation choice -- any spec-conformant f64 arithmetic (which Zig's f64 is, using hardware IEEE-754 doubles) produces exactly this behaviour by construction, with no vendor discretion involved. So the R-Co-access gap that justified treating this as an open question does not actually block implementing the signed/NaN split correctly: no amount of R-Co source access could reveal a DIFFERENT correct answer here, only confirm this one. Combined with the fact that design doc §4.3/§4.6 already fully specifies the 3-way split (the `infinity_marker :: :infinity | :neg_infinity | :nan` type, the per-operator dividend-sign table, and the 5-clause ordering-comparison guard order: nil-check, :nan guard, infinity-marker branch, is_number guard, type-mismatch fallback) -- this is not new invention or scope creep, it is unblocking an already-approved, already-detailed design section that was withheld pending exactly this sign-off -- and given the concrete, demonstrated real-world consequence (a wrong gateway-branch decision on a tenant's own negative-amount data), the unsigned-only fallback is not acceptable as REQ-197's final shape. AC4's literal wording ("float division by zero produces infinity") does not require this fix, but the demonstrated correctness gap does.

PARSE_STRICT/1 TOKENIZER-DUPLICATION VERDICT -- ACCEPT as a reasonable tradeoff, not a cleanup blocker. ELIXIR-DEV's stated rationale (expr.ex:401-418) -- avoiding any risk to `do_tokenize/2`'s escape-handling code, which carries two prior bug-fix histories (ISS-0086, ISS-0087), and guaranteeing `parse/1`'s outer shape and evaluate_condition/2's call graph stay byte-for-byte safe -- is sound engineering judgment for a security-adjacent parsing path, not laziness dressed up as caution: the design doc's own stated preference (share one tokenizer/grammar) is a style preference, not an AC or an invariant, and correctness-risk avoidance is a legitimate reason to deviate from it. This is duplication debt worth watching, not fixing now: `parse_strict/1` is confirmed inert on the gateway-evaluation path today (SECURITY-REVIEWER's call-graph trace, independently spot-checked), so there is no live correctness risk from the two copies silently diverging yet. If `do_tokenize/2` needs a third escape-handling bug fix (ISS-0086/ISS-0087-shaped) before `parse_strict/1` gets a real caller, that fix must be applied to both copies or the two entry points will produce different asts for the same malformed input -- worth a follow-up consolidation once a real caller exists, not before.

OQ-4 (negative-operand integer div/mod truncate-toward-zero direction) -- AWARENESS ACKNOWLEDGED, no action required. Low-risk, reuses Elixir's native div/2 and rem/2 with no new type/AST surface, no AC depends on it; a future R-Co-source-access audit should confirm the rounding direction before this is treated as ported rather than reasoned, per the design doc's own §12 framing.

DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY -- confirmed nothing in docs/migration/decisions/ needs touching: this diff introduces no framework/library choice, no new abstraction ahead of what REQ-197 needs (§4.3/§4.6's extension is a data-representation fix within the already-scoped arithmetic feature, not new machinery ahead of a stage), and no decision record bears on float-arithmetic sign semantics.

No type-safety-gap issue filed: the value()/ast() union's dynamic-atom-mixed-with-number() shape is an established pattern inherited from REQ-050, not a new class of representable-invalid-state introduced by this diff specifically; extending infinity_marker() from 1 to 3 atom variants (the rework this FAIL requests) does not by itself create a new unrepresentable-state gap worth a struct/Ecto.Enum change beyond what a plain closed atom union already provides.

VERDICT: FAIL. Route back to ELIXIR-DEV to implement design §4.3/§4.6's signed-infinity/NaN 3-way split (the design's own already-specified content, unblocked by this sign-off) plus its dependent comparison/negation branches and new AC-level test coverage. Do not re-dispatch to TEST-DESIGNER until this rework lands and re-passes this gate.

issues.description: apply_float_arith(:div, _l, r) when r == 0.0 (expr.ex:1088) and apply_ordering/3's :infinity-is-greatest branch (expr.ex:1109-1115) together make `amount / 0.0 > threshold`-shaped gateway conditions evaluate true for both a large positive AND a large-magnitude negative amount, where correct IEEE-754 signed semantics would place the negative case at -infinity (false). REVIEWER investigated whether R-Co-source unavailability (the reason OQ-1 was left open) actually blocks a fix and found it does not: IEEE-754 division-by-zero sign/NaN rules are a fixed standard, not an R-Co-specific choice, and design doc §4.3/§4.6 already fully specifies the exact fix (infinity_marker() extended to :infinity | :neg_infinity | :nan, per-operator dividend-sign table, 5-clause ordering-comparison guard order). Fix: implement design §4.3's signed-infinity/NaN split and §4.6's dependent :nan/infinity-marker comparison branches exactly as already specified, add apply_neg/1's :neg_infinity/:nan clauses (§4.4), and add new tests for: positive-dividend/zero-divisor -> :infinity (already covered), negative-dividend/zero-divisor -> :neg_infinity, 0.0/0.0 -> :nan, and at least one ordering-comparison test demonstrating the previously-wrong sign-flip case now resolves correctly (e.g. a negative amount divided by a zero divisor compared with `<` a positive threshold now yields true, not false).

result.next_action: Rework ELIXIR-DEV -- 1 BLOCKER above (OQ-1: implement design §4.3/§4.6's already-specified signed-infinity/NaN 3-way split, now unblocked by this sign-off). Carry forward unchanged: OQ-4 (awareness only, no action) and the parse_strict/1 tokenizer-duplication design-preference deviation (accepted as a reasonable tradeoff, not a cleanup blocker, until parse_strict/1 gets a real caller). Once reworked, re-dispatch to REVIEWER (this same gate) for re-check before TEST-DESIGNER.
